title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: For each positive integer \(n,\) the mean of the first \(n\) terms of a sequence is \(n.\) What is the \(2008\)th term of the sequence?

solutions.text:
Since the mean of the first \(n\) terms is \(n,\) their sum is \(n \cdot n = n^2.\)

The \(n\)th term is the difference of consecutive sums, \(n^2 - (n-1)^2 = 2n - 1.\)

For \(n = 2008,\) the term is \(2 \cdot 2008 - 1 = 4015.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: If the mean of the first \(n\) terms is \(n,\) then their sum is \(n^2\)
The \(n\)th term equals the sum of the first \(n\) minus the sum of the first \(n - 1\)
